thread.title: Apple OLED-Screen iPhone Production Plans Shrinking

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple OLED-Screen iPhone Production Plans Shrinking
text:
Disappointing sales of Apple 's ( AAPL ) premium-priced OLED-screen iPhone X have prompted Apple to cut production targets for two new OLED models planned for release this fall, a Wall Street firm reported.
X In recent weeks, news reports from Apple's manufacturing supply-chain partners have indicated that Apple has slashed iPhone X production for the first two quarters of the year.
Cowen analyst Karl Ackerman echoed those observations in a report Tuesday, but said Apple also is pulling back on production targets for its second-generation OLED iPhones, which are likely to be announced in September.
Cowen now expects Apple to make 21 million iPhone X units in the March quarter, down from its prior view of 28.5 million, based on supply-chain checks.
For the June quarter, Apple is likely to procure 13 million to 16 million iPhone X handsets, down from its original plan of 30 million units, Ackerman said.
Apple is expected to release three new iPhones in the fall, including 5.8-inch and 6.5-inch OLED-screen models as well as a 6-inch LCD-screen model.
"Our fieldwork has noticed a shift in procurement plans toward the lower-priced 6-inch (thin-film-transistor) LCD model," Ackerman said. Apple is likely to procure 75 million to 85 million units of the LCD phone, up from a prior target of 55 million to 60 million, he said.
Apple plans to procure 100 million to 120 million units of the two OLED models in the 12th-generation iPhone cycle, he said. That's down from a target of 120 million to 140 million units just a month ago, Ackerman said.
"This is the build (target), but of course actual shipments could change materially from now through the end of the cycle in fall 2019," he said.
